content:
Yesterday's announcement of the Mac Studio featuring the M5 Max chip came with a pleasant surprise: the starting price remains the same as the previous-generation M4 Max Mac Studio, at US$2,499.

However, if you want to upgrade the GPU, watch out for a hidden cost—the actual price is US$300 more than what Apple initially shows on its website…

This hidden upgrade fee also tripped up John Gruber when he was summing up the pricing for the various configurations of the new machines.

The base configuration of this machine comes with an 18-core CPU and 32-core GPU. Apple then lists the option to upgrade to a 40-core GPU, with the price clearly marked at an additional US$300.

The catch is that when you select this option, the memory is also automatically changed from 32GB to 48GB, costing an extra US$300. Since you cannot upgrade the GPU cores alone while keeping the original memory, the actual upgrade cost is double the listed price, coming to US$600.

Apple's explanation regarding this is worded in a slightly vague manner when you select the chip upgrade.

Are you interested in picking up the new Mac mini or Mac Studio? Let us know in the comments.
